title: Current continuity, Drude obstructions and conditional diffusion

items.title: Local charge current and finite-volume correlation conventions
items.design_state: Step 1 assigned design item; current authored draft.
items.statement:
Fix either a finite open chain with sites $\{1,\ldots,L\}$, $L\ge2$, or a periodic chain with sites $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$, $L\ge3$, and denote its site set by $\Lambda_L$. Let $\mathcal H_L$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. For each site $j$, let $q_j=q_j^*$ be a bounded charge observable, with physical unit $\mathsf Q$. For each oriented nearest-neighbor bond $(j,j+1)$, let $h_{j,j+1}=h_{j,j+1}^*$ be an energy operator in joules. Require $[h_{k,k+1},q_j]=0$ whenever $j\notin\{k,k+1\}$, and require local charge conservation $[h_{j,j+1},q_j+q_{j+1}]=0$. On an open chain set $H_L=\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}h_{j,j+1}$; on a ring set $H_L=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z}h_{j,j+1}$ with periodic indices. For an open chain define the absent boundary currents $j_{0,1}=j_{L,L+1}=0$. Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. These finite local data may be realized on a tensor-product spin space or on a finite fixed-particle site space, provided the stated commutation conditions hold.

The oriented bond current from $j$ to $j+1$ is
$$j_{j,j+1}:=\frac{i}{\hbar}[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}].$$
It has unit $\mathsf Q\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The total current is the sum over existing bonds, $J_L:=\sum_{(j,j+1)}j_{j,j+1}$, and its Heisenberg evolution for $t\in\mathbb R$ is $J_L(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_Le^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. For finite inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, define $\rho_{\beta,L}:=e^{-\beta H_L}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_L})$ and $\omega_{\beta,L}(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\beta,L}A)$. Write $J_L^\circ:=J_L-\omega_{\beta,L}(J_L)I$ and $J_L^\circ(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_L^\circ e^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. Define the real, connected, symmetrized correlation per site by
$$C_L(t):=\frac{1}{L}\operatorname{Re}\,\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ\right)=\frac{1}{2L}\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ+J_L^\circ J_L^\circ(t)\right).$$
The correlation has unit $\mathsf Q^2\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ per site.

This definition assigns no transport coefficient by itself. Any proposed finite-volume or thermodynamic transport quantity must additionally state its time cutoff, frequency regulator (for example $e^{-\eta t}$ with $\eta>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$), spatial normalization, and the exact order in which $L\to\infty$, the time cutoff tends to infinity, and any regulator is removed. Existence of those limits is not part of this definition.

items.title: Continuity equation for a local lattice charge current
items.design_state: Step 1 locally added intermediate lemma; complete proof authored.
items.statement:
Use the finite open or periodic chain and bond-current definition in [[def-qsmx-lattice-current-and-limits]]. Each $j_{j,j+1}$ is self-adjoint, and with $\dot q_j:=(i/\hbar)[H_L,q_j]$ the exact local identity
$$\dot q_j=j_{j-1,j}-j_{j,j+1}$$
holds at every site. Consequently the total charge $Q_L:=\sum_{j\in\Lambda_L}q_j$, where $\Lambda_L$ is the open-chain site set or periodic site set from the definition, is conserved: $[H_L,Q_L]=0$. The current orientation is from $j$ to $j+1$, so positive outgoing current lowers the charge at site $j$.

items.title: Conserved overlaps bound the finite persistent current correlation
items.design_state: Step 1 assigned design item; current authored draft.
items.statement:
Take the finite-chain data of the current definition on $\mathcal H_L$ and identify $\mathcal H:=\mathcal H_L$. Let $H=H^*$ have energy unit joules, let $\hbar>0$ have unit joule-seconds, and let $\rho$ be a positive-definite trace-one matrix satisfying $[\rho,H]=0$. Define $\omega(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ and $\alpha_t(A):=e^{iHt/\hbar}Ae^{-iHt/\hbar}$. Let $J_L$ be the total lattice current of the finite-volume current definition and center it with respect to this same $\rho$, setting $J:=J_L-\omega(J_L)I$. With no identification of $H$ and $H_L$, the estimate below is an abstract bound for this observable under $\alpha_t$. Its lattice-transport specialization further takes $H=H_L$; then the Gibbs density $\rho_{\beta,L}$ in that definition is stationary and is an admissible choice of $\rho$. More generally, $\rho_{\beta,L}$ can be used with another $H$ exactly when it also satisfies $[\rho_{\beta,L},H]=0$. Then $J=J^*$, as established by the local continuity result. For $m\ge1$, let $Q_1,\ldots,Q_m$ be linearly independent conserved matrices, $[H,Q_a]=0$. Put
$$G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho Q_a^*Q_b),\qquad v_a:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho Q_a^*J).$$
Then $G$ is positive definite, the finite Cesàro limit exists, and
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\int_0^T\operatorname{Re}\,\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(J)J\right)\,dt\;\ge\;v^*G^{-1}v\;\ge0.$$
This is a finite-dimensional persistent-correlation bound. It does not identify a thermodynamic Drude weight or assert that either volume/time order of limits exists.

items.title: Integrable current correlations give a conditional variance coefficient
items.design_state: Step 1 assigned design item; current authored draft.
items.statement:
Fix a spatial normalization and current convention as in the finite-volume lattice-current definition. Let $C:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a real, even, connected autocorrelation for that specified normalized current. In the classical alternative, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space and let $t\mapsto J(t)$ be a norm-continuous map into the real Hilbert space $L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$. Assume it is centered and second-order stationary, meaning $\mathbb E[J(t)]=0$ and $\mathbb E[J(s)J(t)]=C(t-s)$ for all $s,t\ge0$, with the even extension $C(-u)=C(u)$. Define $X_T:=\int_0^T J(t)\,dt$ as a Bochner integral in $L^2$. In this classical alternative assume $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_0^R|C(t)|\,dt<\infty$ as an absolute improper Riemann integral. In the quantum alternative, let $V=V^*$ be the chosen spatially normalized current observable in a finite-range spin $C^*$-dynamical system with the exact hypotheses of the finite quantum variance theorem cited below, and let its invariant state $\phi$ satisfy $\phi(V)=0$. For its strongly continuous dynamics $\alpha_t$, define $X_T:=\int_0^T\alpha_t(V)\,dt$ as a norm-Riemann integral and $C(t):=\operatorname{Re}\phi(V\alpha_t(V))$. Invariance and self-adjointness make this real correlation even. This quantum alternative assumes exactly the Countable Choice, finite-matrix $C^*$-identity, interaction, state, and dynamics hypotheses in that supplier, and requires $C\in L^1([0,\infty))$ with respect to Lebesgue measure. In either alternative, the corresponding integral being finite gives
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X_T)}{2T}=\int_0^\infty C(t)\,dt=:D\ge0,$$
where the classical variance is $\mathbb E[(X_T-\mathbb E X_T)^2]=\mathbb E[X_T^2]$ and the quantum variance is $\phi(X_T^2)$. The correlation already includes the chosen spatial normalization; if it is obtained from a finite-volume sequence, convergence to $C$ and the order of spatial, time, and frequency-regulator limits are assumptions, not conclusions here. If the chosen current observable $J$ or $V$ has units $\mathsf Q\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, both sides have units $\mathsf Q^2\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, multiplied by any declared spatial-normalization unit. This conditional variance coefficient is not by itself an empirical diffusion constant or a conductivity.

items.title: A conserved finite current obstructs an integrable dc correlation
items.design_state: Step 1 assigned design item; current authored draft.
items.statement: Every finite thermal lattice current correlation $C_L(t)$ defined by the current convention in this page is absolutely integrable on $[0,\infty)$, so its unregulated Green–Kubo integral is finite.
